title: HomeGuard Homeowners Policy Billing Rules: Installment Schedule by Billing Plan
content:
Each term's premium on the HomeGuard Homeowners Policy is billed on the installment schedule of the policy's billing plan.

## Schedule constants

| Billing plan | Installments per term | Interval between due dates |
|---|---|---|
| Annual | 1 | 0 months (single installment) |
| Two-pay | 2 | 6 calendar months |
| Quarterly | 4 | 3 calendar months |
| Monthly EFT | 12 | 1 calendar month |
| Mortgagee escrow | 1 | 0 months (single installment) |

Every installment after the first is posted (billed) **20** days before its due date.

## Due dates

- Installment 1 is due on the term effective date.
- Each later installment is due the plan's interval of calendar months after the previous due date. When that day does not exist in the month reached, the due date falls back to the last day of that month.

## Installment amounts

Each later installment equals the term premium divided by the plan's installment count, rounded half-up to the cent. Installment 1 takes the difference: it is the term premium less the sum of all the later installments, so that the installments add up exactly to the term premium.

## Posting dates

| Installment | Posted on |
|---|---|
| Installment 1 of a new policy | the bound date |
| Installment 1 of a renewal term | the package's renewal offer lead time (in days) before the expiration date of the expiring term |
| Every later installment | 20 days before its due date |

## Mortgagee escrow

Under the mortgagee escrow plan the whole term premium is billed as one installment with the mortgagee as payer, and a mortgagee invoice for the same amount and due date is sent at the same time. No installment fee, late fee or returned-payment fee applies to a mortgagee-billed term.

## Conditions on billing an installment

- **Policy status.** Installments are billed only while the policy is bound, in force, pending cancellation or pending nonrenewal, as the policy record shows. A cancelled or expired policy is not billed.
- **Once only.** An installment that has already been billed for the same term and installment number is never billed again. The term is identified by its term effective date, so the same installment number of a different term is a different installment.

## Hypothetical worked figures

*Hypothetical monthly EFT term premium of 1234.57.* 1234.57 divided by 12 is 102.8808…, rounded half-up to 102.88 for each of installments 2 to 12. Those eleven installments total 1131.68, so installment 1 is 1234.57 less 1131.68, which is 102.89.

*Hypothetical quarterly term premium of 1450.00.* 1450.00 divided by 4 is 362.50 exactly; installments 2 to 4 are 362.50 each and installment 1 is 1450.00 less 1087.50, which is 362.50.

*Hypothetical two-pay term effective 31 August.* Installment 1 is due 31 August. Installment 2 is due six calendar months later; 31 February does not exist, so it falls back to the last day of February. It is posted 20 days before that due date.
